API gateway never records downstream failures into the circuit breaker, so the breaker never opens
rejectionReason: The breaker records downstream failures itself: the gateway wraps every call in `breaker.call(...)`, and `CircuitBreaker.call` invokes `_onFailure()` on exhausted attempts, which increments `failureCount` and opens the circuit at `failureThreshold`. No separate failure-recording in the gateway is needed (or correct); a persistently failing adapter does open the breaker.
body:
## Description (rejected)

The suspected finding claims `ApiGateway` "never records downstream failures into the circuit breaker, so the breaker never opens." Reading the code shows this is not a defect.

`ApiGateway.execute` routes every downstream call through the per-service breaker:

```typescript
const breaker = this.breakers.get(serviceId)!;
const rawResponse = await breaker.call(() => adapter.execute<T>(req, credential));
```

(`packages/integrations/src/api-gateway.ts:141-143`)

Failure accounting is the breaker's own responsibility inside `call`. When `fn()` throws and the internal retry loop is exhausted, `CircuitBreaker.call` calls `this._onFailure()` (`packages/integrations/src/circuit-breaker.ts:144`), which increments `failureCount` and opens the circuit once `failureCount >= failureThreshold` (`packages/integrations/src/circuit-breaker.ts:175-189`). The gateway therefore does not need to — and must not — record failures separately, because doing so would double-count.

## Impact

None. A persistently failing adapter does cause the breaker to open via the existing `breaker.call(...)` path, so the stated reliability gap does not exist.

## Required Fix

No fix required for this item. (A genuinely related, narrower defect — that the breaker fires only one `_onFailure` per `call` after exhausting its internal retries, and that HALF_OPEN runs a multi-attempt burst rather than a single probe — is captured separately under `integ-circuit-breaker-half-open-full-retry-loop`.)

## References

- Verified against `packages/integrations/src/api-gateway.ts:124-153` and `packages/integrations/src/circuit-breaker.ts:119-190`.

title: HTTP adapter follows redirects while forwarding the Authorization header to the redirect target
body:
## Description

`HttpBaseAdapter.execute` builds a header set that includes the credential-derived auth headers (typically `Authorization`) and then calls the global `fetch` with the default redirect behaviour:

```typescript
const headers: Record<string, string> = {
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
  ...this.defaultHeaders,
  ...this.buildAuthHeaders(credential),   // e.g. { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` }
  ...(request.headers ?? {}),
};
// ...
const response = await fetch(url, {
  method: request.method,
  headers,
  body: request.body !== undefined ? JSON.stringify(request.body) : undefined,
  signal: controller.signal,
});
```

No `redirect` option is passed, so `fetch` uses its default of `"follow"` and transparently follows 3xx responses. This project runs on Node `>=20` (`package.json` `engines.node`) using the built-in `fetch` (undici). Unlike browsers — which strip `Authorization` on cross-origin redirects per the Fetch standard — Node's `fetch`/undici does **not** strip the `Authorization` header when following a redirect to a different origin. The `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` header (and any other secret in `defaultHeaders`) is therefore re-sent verbatim to whatever host the upstream 3xx `Location` points at.

## Impact

If an upstream endpoint is compromised or attacker-influenced (open redirect, misconfiguration, or a malicious/MITM'd intermediary), it can return a 3xx pointing at an attacker-controlled host and the adapter will resend the bearer token / API key to that host — a credential-leak to an arbitrary third party. Because the adapter is the shared base for every service adapter behind the `ApiGateway`, this exposure applies to all outbound integrations. Medium severity: requires a redirect from (or injected into) an upstream response, but the consequence is disclosure of long-lived service credentials.

## Required Fix

1. Set `redirect: "manual"` (or `"error"`) on the `fetch` call and handle 3xx explicitly: only follow redirects to the same origin as `this.meta.baseUrl`, and strip `Authorization`/secret headers before following a cross-origin redirect.
2. If redirect-following is required, re-derive auth headers per hop based on the target origin rather than blindly forwarding the original headers.
3. Add a test with a mock that 3xx-redirects to a different origin and asserts the `Authorization` header is not sent to the redirect target.

## References

- OWASP A01:2021 – Broken Access Control (covers unvalidated redirects/forwards) — https://owasp.org/Top10/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/
- CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html
- CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect) — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html
